1	# Rulebook file format
2	
3	How to write a scheme so the engine can apply it and people can audit it. The example below is a made-up scheme; its numbers are not real.
4	
5	## 1. Register the source document: `sources/index.yaml`
6	
7	```yaml
8	gr-202501011200000000:
9	  kind: government_resolution
10	  code: "202501011200000000"
11	  date: 2025-01-01
12	  department: Example Department, Government of Maharashtra
13	  title_mr: <title in Marathi as printed>
14	  title_en: <English title>
15	  url: https://gr.maharashtra.gov.in/Site/Upload/Government%20Resolutions/Marathi/202501011200000000.pdf
16	  local: sources/mh/202501011200000000.pdf
17	  language: mr
18	```
19	
20	## 2. The scheme: `schemes/mh/<scheme_name>.yaml`
21	
22	```yaml
23	id: mh.example_support            # mh.<snake_case_name>
24	name: Example Support Yojana       # official name in English letters
25	name_mr: <name in Marathi>
26	department: Example Department, Government of Maharashtra
27	summary: One plain-English sentence on who gets what.
28	launched: 2025-01-01               # date of the founding order
29	apply_url: https://example.gov.in/  # optional
30	benefit:
31	  monthly_inr: "params.monthly_amount"      # expression; may use person and params
32	  source: {doc: gr-202501011200000000, page: 2, clause: "3", quote: "<exact words>", quote_en: "<translation>"}
33	conditions:                        # every condition must be true to be eligible
34	  - id: resident
35	    text: Lives in Maharashtra     # plain English; {param_name} is replaced by the value
36	    when: "person.state == 'MH'"   # expression over person.<field> and params.<name>
37	    valid_from: 2025-01-01
38	    source: {doc: gr-202501011200000000, page: 2, clause: "4(1)", quote: "<exact words>", quote_en: "<translation>"}
39	  - id: age
40	    text: "Aged {age_min} to {age_max}"
41	    when: "params.age_min <= person.age <= params.age_max"
42	    valid_from: 2025-01-01
43	    source: {...}
44	  - id: no_tax_payer
45	    kind: disqualification         # optional label for rules that exclude people
46	    text: No one in the family pays income tax
47	    when: "not person.family_income_tax_payer"
48	    valid_from: 2025-01-01
49	    source: {...}
50	```
51	
52	Expressions may use only `person.<field>` (fields listed in `schema/person.yaml`), `params.<name>`, comparisons (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `in`, `not in`, chained like `a <= x <= b`), `and`, `or`, `not`, `+ - * /`, lists `[...]`, and `min`, `max`, `abs`, `len`.
53	
54	## 3. Parameters: `parameters/mh/<scheme_name>/<param_name>.yaml`
55	
56	One file per changeable number or list. Values are dated; never edit or delete old values, add new dates.
57	
58	```yaml
59	description: Maximum age in completed years
60	metadata:
61	  unit: year
62	values:
63	  2025-01-01:

147	        out = {}
148	        for name, spec in self.person_schema.items():
149	            value = person.get(name, spec.get("default"))
150	            if value is None:
151	                out[name] = None
152	                continue
153	            kind = spec.get("type")
154	            if kind == "int":
155	                value = int(value)
156	            elif kind == "number":
157	                value = float(value)
158	            elif kind == "bool":
159	                value = value if isinstance(value, bool) else str(value).lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}

171	        on = _to_date(on) if on else dt.date.today()
172	        p = self.normalise_person(person)
173	        results = {}
174	        for sid, scheme in self.schemes.items():
175	            if schemes and sid not in schemes:
176	                continue
177	            launched = _to_date(scheme.data["launched"])
178	            closed = scheme.data.get("closed")
179	            if on < launched or (closed and on > _to_date(closed)):
180	                results[sid] = {"eligible": False, "in_force": False, "monthly_inr": 0, "reasons": []}
181	                continue
182	            params = scheme.params_at(on)
183	            reasons = []
184	            for c in scheme.conditions:

188	                reasons.append({

191	                    "met": met,

197	            if eligible and benefit:

206	        def fmt(v: Any) -> str:
207	            if isinstance(v, list):

209	            if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v >= 1000:

214	        except (KeyError, IndexError):

218	    def rules_at(self, scheme_id: str, on: dt.date | str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
219	        on = _to_date(on) if on else dt.date.today()
220	        s = self.schemes[scheme_id]
221	        params = s.params_at(on)
222	        return {
223	            "id": s.id,
224	            "name": s.name,
225	            "as_of": on.isoformat(),
226	            "conditions": [
227	                {"id": c.id, "text": self.render_text(c.text, params), "when": c.when,
228	                 "source": c.source, "valid_from": c.valid_from.isoformat(),
229	                 "valid_until": c.valid_until.isoformat() if c.valid_until else None}
230	                for c in s.conditions if c.active(on)
231	            ],
232	            "parameters": {
233	                name: {"value": v.value, "since": v.start.isoformat(), "reference": v.reference,
234	                       "description": s.params[name].description, "unit": s.params[name].unit}
235	                for name in s.params if (v := s.params[name].at(on))
236	            },
237	        }
238	
239	    def check(self) -> list[str]:
240	        """Structural validation. Returns a list of problems (empty means valid)."""
241	        problems = []
242	        for sid, s in self.schemes.items():
243	            for key in ("name", "launched", "department", "summary"):
244	                if key not in s.data:
245	                    problems.append(f"{sid}: missing '{key}'")
246	            ids = [c.id for c in s.conditions]
247	            for c in s.conditions:
248	                where = f"{sid}.{c.id}"
249	                for need in ("doc", "page", "quote"):
250	                    if not c.source.get(need):
251	                        problems.append(f"{where}: source is missing '{need}'")
252	                if c.source.get("doc") and c.source["doc"] not in self.sources:
253	                    problems.append(f"{where}: source doc '{c.source['doc']}' is not in sources/index.yaml")
254	                if c.valid_until and c.valid_until < c.valid_from:
255	                    problems.append(f"{where}: valid_until is before valid_from")
256	                try:
257	                    for root, attr in names_used(c.when):
258	                        if root == "person" and attr not in self.person_schema:
259	                            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown person field '{attr}'")
260	                        if root == "params" and attr not in s.params:
261	                            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown parameter '{attr}'")
262	                except RuleExpressionError as e:
263	                    problems.append(f"{where}: {e}")
264	            for cid in set(ids):
265	                periods = sorted((c.valid_from, c.valid_until or dt.date.max) for c in s.conditions if c.id == cid)
266	                for (a0, a1), (b0, _) in zip(periods, periods[1:]):
267	                    if b0 <= a1:
268	                        problems.append(f"{sid}.{cid}: overlapping validity periods")
269	            for name, p in s.params.items():
270	                if not p.values:
271	                    problems.append(f"{sid}: parameter '{name}' has no values")
272	                for v in p.values:
273	                    ref = v.reference or {}
274	                    if not ref.get("doc"):
275	                        problems.append(f"{sid}: parameter '{name}' value from {v.start} has no reference doc")
276	        return problems

1	"""A tiny, whitelisted expression evaluator for rule conditions.
2	
3	Rule files are edited by an AI agent, so they must never be able to run
4	arbitrary Python. Only comparisons, boolean logic, arithmetic, attribute
5	access on `person` and `params`, literals and a few pure functions are allowed.
6	"""

8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import ast
11	import operator
12	from typing import Any
13	
14	_BIN_OPS = {
15	    ast.Add: operator.add,
16	    ast.Sub: operator.sub,
17	    ast.Mult: operator.mul,
18	    ast.Div: operator.truediv,
19	}
20	_CMP_OPS = {
21	    ast.Eq: operator.eq,
22	    ast.NotEq: operator.ne,
23	    ast.Lt: operator.lt,
24	    ast.LtE: operator.le,
25	    ast.Gt: operator.gt,
26	    ast.GtE: operator.ge,
27	    ast.In: lambda a, b: a in b,
28	    ast.NotIn: lambda a, b: a not in b,
29	}
30	_FUNCS = {"min": min, "max": max, "abs": abs, "len": len}
31	_ROOTS = {"person", "params"}
32	
33	
34	class RuleExpressionError(ValueError):
35	    pass
36	
37	
38	class Namespace:
39	    """Attribute access over a dict, with a clear error for unknown names."""
40	
41	    def __init__(self, label: str, values: dict[str, Any]):
42	        self._label = label
43	        self._values = values
44	
45	    def get(self, name: str) -> Any:
46	        if name not in self._values:
47	            raise RuleExpressionError(f"unknown {self._label} field '{name}'")
48	        return self._values[name]
49	
50	
51	def names_used(expr: str) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
52	    """Return {(root, attribute)} pairs referenced by an expression."""
53	    tree = _parse(expr)
54	    used = set()
55	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
56	        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name):
57	            used.add((node.value.id, node.attr))
58	    return used
59	
60	
61	def _parse(expr: str) -> ast.Expression:
62	    try:
63	        tree = ast.parse(expr, mode="eval")
64	    except SyntaxError as e:
65	        raise RuleExpressionError(f"invalid expression {expr!r}: {e.msg}") from e
66	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
67	        allowed = (
68	            ast.Expression, ast.BoolOp, ast.And, ast.Or, ast.UnaryOp, ast.Not, ast.USub,
69	            ast.BinOp, ast.Compare, ast.Name, ast.Attribute, ast.Constant, ast.List,
70	            ast.Tuple, ast.Load, ast.Call, ast.IfExp,
71	            *_BIN_OPS.keys(), *_CMP_OPS.keys(),
72	        )
73	        if not isinstance(node, allowed):
74	            raise RuleExpressionError(f"'{type(node).__name__}' is not allowed in rule expressions")
75	        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id not in _ROOTS | set(_FUNCS) | {"True", "False", "None"}:
76	            raise RuleExpressionError(f"unknown name '{node.id}'")
77	        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
78	            if not (isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in _FUNCS) or node.keywords:
79	                raise RuleExpressionError("only min, max, abs and len may be called")
80	        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and not (isinstance(node.value, ast.Name) and node.value.id in _ROOTS):
81	            raise RuleExpressionError("attributes are only allowed on person and params")
82	    return tree
83	
84	
85	def evaluate(expr: str, person: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
86	    tree = _parse(expr)
87	    env = {"person": Namespace("person", person), "params": Namespace("parameter", params)}
88	    return _eval(tree.body, env)
89	
90	
91	def _eval(node: ast.AST, env: dict[str, Namespace]) -> Any:
92	    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant):
93	        return node.value
94	    if isinstance(node, (ast.List, ast.Tuple)):
95	        return [_eval(e, env) for e in node.elts]
96	    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
97	        return env[node.value.id].get(node.attr)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
98	    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
99	        return {"True": True, "False": False, "None": None}[node.id]
100	    if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
101	        if isinstance(node.op, ast.And):
102	            return all(_eval(v, env) for v in node.values)
103	        return any(_eval(v, env) for v in node.values)
104	    if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
105	        val = _eval(node.operand, env)
106	        return (not val) if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not) else -val
107	    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
108	        return _BIN_OPS[type(node.op)](_eval(node.left, env), _eval(node.right, env))
109	    if isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
110	        left = _eval(node.left, env)
111	        for op, comp in zip(node.ops, node.comparators):
112	            right = _eval(comp, env)
113	            if not _CMP_OPS[type(op)](left, right):
114	                return False
115	            left = right
116	        return True
117	    if isinstance(node, ast.IfExp):
118	        return _eval(node.body, env) if _eval(node.test, env) else _eval(node.orelse, env)
119	    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
120	        return _FUNCS[node.func.id](*[_eval(a, env) for a in node.args])  # type: ignore[union-attr]
121	    raise RuleExpressionError(f"cannot evaluate {type(node).__name__}")

## 1 September 2019: Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana (GR dated 20 August 2019)

- English: The scheme starts on 1 September 2019 with revised rules. People who have lived in Maharashtra for at least 15 years, are aged 18 to 64, have a family income up to Rs 21,000 a year (Rs 50,000 for disabled people), and get no regular benefit from another government scheme, get Rs 1,000 a month. Widows with one child get Rs 1,100 and widows with two or more children get Rs 1,200.
- हिंदी: संजय गांधी निराधार अनुदान योजना 1 सितंबर 2019 से संशोधित नियमों के साथ शुरू होती है। जो व्यक्ति महाराष्ट्र में कम से कम 15 वर्ष से रह रहे हैं, 18 से 64 वर्ष की आयु के हैं, जिनके परिवार की वार्षिक आय 21,000 रुपये तक है (दिव्यांगों के लिए 50,000 रुपये), और किसी अन्य सरकारी योजना से नियमित मासिक लाभ नहीं लेते, उन्हें हर महीने 1,000 रुपये मिलेंगे। एक अपत्य वाली विधवाओं को 1,100 रुपये और दो या अधिक अपत्य वाली विधवाओं को 1,200 रुपये मिलेंगे।
- मराठी: संजय गांधी निराधार अनुदान योजना १ सप्टेंबर २०१९ पासून सुधारित नियमांसह सुरू होत आहे. महाराष्ट्रात किमान १५ वर्षांपासून रहिवासी, १८ ते ६४ वयोगटातील, ज्यांचे कुटुंबाचे वार्षिक उत्पन्न २१,००० रुपयांपर्यंत आहे (दिव्यांगांसाठी ५०,००० रुपये) आणि इतर कोणत्याही शासकीय योजनेतून नियमित मासिक लाभ घेत नाहीत, त्यांना दरमहा १,००० रुपये मिळतील. एक अपत्य असलेल्या विधवांना १,१०० रुपये आणि दोन किंवा अधिक अपत्ये असलेल्या विधवांना १,२०० रुपये मिळतील.

The Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar scheme is now in the rulebook. `python -m niyam_rulebook test` prints `tests: 49 passed, 0 failed` with no PROBLEM lines (25 existing Ladki Bahin cases, 24 new).

**What I added**
- **Scheme:** `schemes/mh/sanjay_gandhi_niradhar.yaml`. Five conditions: Maharashtra residence for 15 years, age 18 or more, age under 65, family income limit, and no regular benefit from another scheme. Each has its quote and page from the change set. The benefit is Rs 1,000, or Rs 1,100 for a widow with one child and Rs 1,200 for a widow with two or more.
- **Parameters:** five files under `parameters/mh/sanjay_gandhi_niradhar/`: the monthly amounts and the two income limits. All are dated 2019-09-01 and cite the GR.
- **Tests:** `tests/mh/sanjay_gandhi_niradhar.yaml`, 24 cases covering each limit (just below, at, just above), the widow amounts, and a case dated 2019-08-31 showing the scheme is not in force yet.
- **Schema:** three new person fields, each with a default that keeps people eligible: `years_in_maharashtra` (default 15), `children_count` (default 0), and `disabled` (default true).
- **Changelog:** an entry at the top in English, Hindi and Marathi, linking the GR.

**Choices to review**
- **`launched` is 2019-09-01**, not the GR date of 2019-08-20. Conditions only start on 1 September, and with an earlier launch date the scheme would report people as eligible before it applies.
- **`disabled` defaults to true**, so when the field is unknown, the higher Rs 50,000 limit applies. That is the default you asked for, but it lets non-disabled families with income up to Rs 50,000 through. Change it if you prefer the stricter reading.
- **The 15-year residence rule** uses the new field, so it is stricter than the change set's literal `state == 'MH'` expression.

**Gaps you should know about before this goes live**
- **Beneficiary categories are not modelled.** The change set skipped them (widows, destitute women, disabled people, and so on). As written, any Maharashtra resident aged 18 to 64 with income under the limit and no other benefit is eligible, including men. This is over-inclusive and needs the category conditions added before anyone relies on the result.
- **The Below Poverty Line (BPL) list is not modelled.** The Rs 21,000 limit applies "if the family is not on the BPL list", and no person field covers that.
- **Two ambiguities from the change set are encoded as written.** The Rs 21,000 limit is inclusive, and any regular benefit from another scheme (including central pensions) disqualifies.
